title: Staged escape-hatch rollback with telemetry bucketing, prefix warmup, and causal state replay
creator: Sanjay Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, staged rollback "escape-hatch" that uses telemetry bucketing and causal state replay to safely revert problematic configuration changes (batching, caching, and routing) with minimal customer impact and predictable cost behavior.

Background: We frequently see config changes (batch size, cache TTLs, routing weights) that improve cost but occasionally produce regressions that require urgent reversal. Current manual rollback is slow and error-prone, and existing automation reverts too broadly or too late. This ticket proposes a middle-ground: a runway of automated mitigations (soft-fallback -> partial rollback -> full rollback) driven by telemetry buckets, with state snapshots for causal replay and a prefix warmup stage to avoid cache cold-start regressions. The solution must be safe for hosted/Dedicated/Private runtimes and integrate with rollout policies in the Console.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace human approvals for high-risk changes (enterprise-only locked flags) and does not add new RBAC models. It focuses on config changes that we auto-deploy via the config apply pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Automated rollback pipeline triggers a staged sequence (soft-fallback -> partial revert -> full revert) when telemetry in target buckets exceeds thresholds
Snapshot and prefix-state capture created before risky config apply and used for causal state replay during verification
KV-cache quarantine and prefix warmup implemented: nodes can be isolated and warmed to avoid cold-start penalties during rollback
Rollbacks complete within SLOs: 90th percentile rollback completion time < 5 minutes for Hosted, < 10 minutes for Dedicated
Post-rollback verification run (synthetic probes + production sampling) shows regression metrics returned within acceptable delta (latency/regressions < 5% above baseline)
Audit trail visible in Console: trigger reason, telemetry buckets, decision path, and PR/Run IDs
Automated tests and integration test harness validate behavior across simulated heavy-batching and cache-thrashing workloads
tasks: Design telemetry bucketing strategy (per-route, per-customer tier, per-region) and thresholds
Implement snapshot capture and store (metadata only + minimal KV prefix state) before apply
Add prefix-warmup flow: on partial rollback, warm a subset of nodes with recorded prefixes before full traffic cutover
Build rollback state machine: soft-fallback -> partial revert -> full revert with configurable hysteresis
Create console UI hooks to display rollback runway steps and allow manual abort/force-commit
Add integration tests & synthetic workloads for cold-start/regression scenarios
Coordinate with reliability on SLO targets and on-call playbook updates
comments: 2026-02-11 - Sanjay Patel: Kickoff doc posted to Confluence; initial design assumes we can snapshot minimal KV prefix state (~1MB) per shard. Need confirmation from storage team that snapshot capture won't block hot paths.

2026-02-18 - Elena Rodriguez: Prototype of state machine merged to feature branch. Soft-fallback implemented as routing to lower-cost model variant plus lowering batch size. Observed 8% latency increase in one synthetic run — tuning thresholds needed.

2026-02-22 - Reliability (Claire Wong): Reviewed SLO targets. Recommend adding a delay window before automatic full revert to avoid oscillation during noisy telemetry. Suggested hysteresis: require two consecutive 2-min windows above threshold.

2026-02-25 - Security (Rajiv Menon): Confirmed no new secrets are stored in snapshots; encryption at rest required for snapshot artifacts. Marking security_review_required=false because we use existing KMS flows.

2026-02-28 - Elena Rodriguez: Added prefix-warmup step to reduce cold-start penalty observed in canary -> full rollback transition. Warmup uses recorded prefixes saved to snapshot; warmed nodes validated by probe traffic.
2026-03-01 - PM (Ariel Bowen): Prioritized visibility: console must show the telemetry bucket that tripped and the decision path. Also requested a manual "step back" button in the Console for SREs.
